result.rationale: Verified in the diff: the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`. The save action nearby does handle errors via `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, so the asymmetry is real and specific. A failed server-side delete (e.g., validation or network error) would leave the row visible with no feedback and an unhandled rejection. This is a substantive error-handling gap rather than a defect on the happy path, so important_non_bug with moderate-high confidence.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in the delete action at line 46, the destroyRecord() promise chain only has a .then() handler but no .catch() handler. If the delete API call fails, the error will be silently swallowed and the row will remain visible without any error message shown to the user. This is inconsistent with the save() action which properly uses .catch(popupAjaxError) to handle errors. This is a real defect in error handling.
